facts.text: The applicant was born in 1968 and lives in Diyarbakır.

anchor.surface_text: 4.  The applicant was born in 1968 and lives in Diyarbakır.

facts.text: On 17 November 1998 at 3.30 p.m. the applicant, a journalist working for a biweekly newspaper, was taken into custody by police officers from the Anti-Terrorist Branch of the Diyarbakır Police Headquarters along with 108 other persons.

anchor.surface_text: 5.  On 17 November 1998 at 3.30 p.m. the applicant, a journalist working for a biweekly newspaper, was taken into custody by police officers from the Anti-Terrorist Branch of the Diyarbakır Police Headquarters along with 108 other persons.

facts.text: At the time of the arrest, the applicant and the other arrestees were in the Diyarbakır branch of the People’s Democracy Party (HADEP), where demonstrations and hunger strikes were allegedly being organised to protest about the arrest of Abdullah Öcalan, the leader of the PKK.

anchor.surface_text: 5.  On 17 November 1998 at 3.30 p.m. the applicant, a journalist working for a biweekly newspaper, was taken into custody by police officers from the Anti-Terrorist Branch of the Diyarbakır Police Headquarters along with 108 other persons. At the time of the arrest, the applicant and the other arrestees were in the Diyarbakır branch of the People’s Democracy Party (HADEP), where demonstrations and hunger strikes were allegedly being organised, in order to protest about the arrest of Abdullah Öcalan, the leader of the PKK (the Workers’ Party of Kurdistan), an illegal organisation.

facts.text: At 7.30 p.m. on 17 November 1998 the applicant was taken to the Diyarbakır State Hospital. The doctor who examined him noted that there was no sign of recent physical violence on the applicant’s person.

anchor.surface_text: 6 At 7.30 p.m. on the same day the applicant was taken to the Diyarbakır State Hospital. The doctor who examined him noted that there was no sign of recent physical violence on the applicant’s person.

facts.text: On 20 November 1998 the applicant made statements to the police, stating he had been in the Diyarbakır branch of HADEP to participate in the demonstration.

anchor.surface_text: 7.  On 20 November 1998 the applicant made statements to the police. According to the report signed by two police officers and the applicant, the applicant stated that he had been in the Diyarbakır branch of HADEP in order to participate in the demonstration.

facts.text: The applicant alleges that he was subjected to various forms of ill-treatment while in police custody, including being kept in a dark cell with insufficient ventilation, deprived of food and water, prevented from going to the toilet, forced to stand handcuffed for long hours, stripped naked, insulted, threatened with death and rape, beaten on various parts of his body including repeated blows to his abdomen, his testicles were squeezed, subjected to sexual abuse, and forced to watch a female detainee being sexually abused.

anchor.surface_text: 8.  The applicant alleges that he was subjected to various forms of ill‑treatment while in police custody. In particular, he was kept in a dark cell with insufficient ventilation, deprived of food and water and was prevented from going to the toilet. He was forced to stand, handcuffed, in the same position for long hours. During the questioning, he was stripped naked, insulted and threatened with death and rape. The applicant was beaten on various parts of his body. In particular, he received repeated blows to his abdomen. His testicles were squeezed and he was subjected to sexual abuse. Finally, he was forced to watch a female detainee being sexually abused.

facts.text: On 23 November 1998 the applicant, along with nine other persons, was taken to a clinic in Diyarbakır and examined by a medical expert who noted that none of them had sustained any injuries.

anchor.surface_text: 9.  On 23 November 1998 the applicant, along with nine other persons, was taken to a clinic in Diyarbakır and examined there by a medical expert, who drafted one document in respect of all ten people, and noted that none of them had sustained any injuries.

facts.text: On 25 November 1998 the applicant, along with 110 other persons, was taken to the same clinic and examined by another doctor, Mr A.O., who noted below every name: 'No sign of physical violence has been observed'.

anchor.surface_text: 10.  On 25 November 1998 the applicant, along with 110 other persons, was taken to the same clinic and examined there by another doctor, Mr A.O. On a document of the police headquarters in which the names of all 111 persons were put, Mr A.O. noted the same sentence below every name: “No sign of physical violence has been observed”.

facts.text: The applicant claimed that police officers were present in the examination room on 25 November 1998 and that although he described the ill-treatment, the doctor did not note any complaints.

anchor.surface_text: The applicant claimed that there had been police officers present in the examination room and that although he had described the type of ill-treatment to which he had been subjected in police custody, the doctor did not note any of his complaints.

facts.text: On 25 November 1998 the applicant was brought before the public prosecutor at the Diyarbakır State Security Court, maintained he was in the HADEP building as a journalist and had not participated in the demonstration or hunger strike, and stated he had been made to sign police statements without reading them.

anchor.surface_text: 11.  On 25 November 1998 the applicant was brought before the public prosecutor at the Diyarbakır State Security Court. He maintained that he had been in the HADEP building as a journalist and that he had not participated in the demonstration or the hunger strike. He stated that he had been made to sign his police statements without reading them.

facts.text: At 9 p.m. on 25 November 1998 the applicant was released upon the decision of the public prosecutor.

anchor.surface_text: 12.  At 9 p.m. on the same day, the applicant was released upon the decision of the public prosecutor.

facts.text: On 26 November 1998 the applicant was examined by a doctor from the Diyarbakır branch of the Human Rights Foundation of Turkey, Mr R.A., who recorded bruises and pain consistent with ill-treatment.

anchor.surface_text: 13.  On 26 November 1998 the applicant was examined by a doctor from the Diyarbakır branch of the Human Rights Foundation of Turkey, Mr R.A., who recorded the following[1]: “There is a bruise measuring 10 x 0.5 cm on the right side of the hypogastrium[2]. He has sensitivity and pain upon palpation behind his knees, pain in the ankles, sensitivity and pain in the toe muscles in both feet. He also has sensitivity in his testicles and epididymis, swelling in the groin (may be the beginning of a hernia), sensitivity and pain in the epigastrium[3]. An eruption on the occipital region has been observed.”

facts.text: Between 7 and 11 December 1998 the applicant underwent various medical examinations at the Izmir branch of the Turkish Medical Association, which concluded he suffered from a hernia, pain, major depression and acute stress disorder consistent with ill-treatment.

anchor.surface_text: 14.  On an unspecified date the Diyarbakır branch of the Human Rights Foundation of Turkey referred the applicant to the Izmir branch of the Turkish Medical Association. Between 7 and 11 December 1998 the applicant underwent various medical examinations, the results of which were noted in a medical report of 4 August 1999. According to this report, the applicant was suffering from a hernia in the groin, pain in various parts of his body and from major depression and an acute stress disorder, two psychiatric conditions that normally are caused by traumatic experiences such as rape and torture. The doctors concluded that the applicant’s complaints were consistent with his allegations of ill-treatment.

facts.text: On 17 December 1998 the applicant underwent surgery for the hernia in his groin, which had allegedly occurred as a result of the ill-treatment he had suffered in police custody.

anchor.surface_text: 15.  On 17 December 1998 the applicant underwent surgery for the hernia in his groin, which had allegedly occurred as a result of the ill-treatment he had suffered in police custody.

facts.text: On 17 January 1999 the applicant drafted a document for his lawyers describing in detail the alleged ill-treatment suffered during police custody between 17 and 25 November 1998 and authorising legal representatives to bring proceedings on his behalf.

anchor.surface_text: 16.  On 17 January 1999[4] the applicant drafted a document for his lawyers in which he described in detail the alleged ill-treatment that he had suffered during his police custody between 17 and 25 November 1998. At the end of the document, he noted that the applicant’s representative before the Court and another advocate would bring proceedings on his behalf as his legal representatives.

facts.text: On 11 May 2000 the applicant’s lawyer lodged a complaint with the Diyarbakır public prosecutor’s office alleging ill-treatment during police custody and submitted a copy of the medical report of 4 August 1999.

anchor.surface_text: 17.  On 11 May 2000 the applicant’s lawyer lodged a complaint with the Diyarbakır public prosecutor’s office that the applicant had been subjected to ill-treatment during his police custody. He submitted a copy of the medical report of 4 August 1999 along with his petition.

facts.text: On 9 January 2002 the Diyarbakır public prosecutor invited the applicant’s representative to make statements.

anchor.surface_text: 18.  On 9 January 2002 the Diyarbakır public prosecutor invited the applicant’s representative to his office in order to make statements.

facts.text: On 10 January 2002 the applicant’s representative made statements to the public prosecutor, contending that the applicant had requested him to initiate proceedings a few days before 11 May 2000 and that the allegations were consistent with the report of 26 November 1998.

anchor.surface_text: 19.  On 10 January 2002 the applicant’s representative made statements to the public prosecutor. He contended that the applicant had requested him to initiate proceedings on his behalf a few days before 11 May 2000[5], the date on which he had lodged a complaint on behalf of the applicant. The representative further noted that the applicant’s allegations were consistent with the findings of the report of 26 November 1998.

facts.text: On 23 January 2002 the Diyarbakır public prosecutor invited the applicant to make statements.

anchor.surface_text: 20.  On 23 January 2002 the Diyarbakır public prosecutor invited the applicant to his office in order to make statements.

facts.text: On 1 February 2002 the applicant made statements to the public prosecutor requesting punishment of the police officers who had ill-treated him.

anchor.surface_text: 21.  On 1 February 2002 the applicant made statements to the public prosecutor. He noted that he had requested his lawyer to lodge a complaint against the persons who had inflicted ill-treatment on him. He contended that his lawyer had told him that he had initiated proceedings. The applicant stated that he had not applied to the public prosecutor’s office himself. He finally requested that the police officers who had ill-treated him be punished.

facts.text: On 1 February 2002 the Diyarbakır public prosecutor issued a decision not to prosecute regarding the applicant’s allegations of ill-treatment, noting no signs of violence in medical reports and that the applicant should have lodged a complaint earlier.

anchor.surface_text: 22.  On the same date the Diyarbakır public prosecutor issued a decision not to prosecute in respect of the applicant’s allegations of ill-treatment. In his decision, the public prosecutor noted that the applicant had been detained in police custody between 17 and 23 November 1998 and that the relevant medical reports did not reveal any sign of violence on the applicant’s person. The public prosecutor further noted that the applicant had applied to the Turkish Medical Association at the end of his custody period and that he should have lodged a complaint with the public prosecutor’s office instead.

facts.text: On 26 February 2002 the applicant’s lawyer lodged an objection with the Siverek Assize Court against the decision not to prosecute, requesting witnesses and medical experts be heard and police officers identified.

anchor.surface_text: 23.  On 26 February 2002 the applicant’s lawyer lodged an objection with the Siverek Assize Court against the Diyarbakır public prosecutor’s decision of 1 February 2002. He requested that persons who had been in police custody at the same time as the applicant be summoned to make statements. He further requested that the doctors who had drawn up the report of 4 August 1999 and Mr A.O., the doctor who had examined the applicant along with 110 other persons on 25 November 1998, be heard. The lawyer also requested that the police officers who had been on duty during the applicant’s detention in custody be determined and the photos of the applicant taken during his detention be included in the file, if there were any.

facts.text: On 14 March 2002 a single judge at the Siverek Assize Court dismissed the applicant’s objection, noting no signs of violence in medical reports and that the applicant had not alleged ill-treatment immediately after detention.

anchor.surface_text: 24.  On 14 March 2002 a single judge at the Siverek Assize Court dismissed the applicant’s objection. In his decision, the judge noted that the applicant had been in police custody between 17 and 23 November 1998 and that the medical report of 23 November 1998, the date on which he was released, did not reveal any sign of violence on the applicant’s person[6]. He further observed that the applicant had not alleged ill‑treatment before the public prosecutor at the Diyarbakır State Security Court on 25 November 1998, immediately after his detention in police custody. The judge finally noted that the applicant had applied to the Turkish Medical Association on 4 August 1999, and had lodged his complaint on 11 May 2000. The judge considered that the applicant’s allegations were dubious, since he had lodged his application a long time after his release from police custody.
Article 3 of the Convention

concepts.interpretation: Article 3 enshrines one of the most fundamental values of democratic societies, making no provision for exceptions, and no derogation from it is permissible under Article 15 § 2 (see Selmouni v. France). The Court found a violation of Article 3 under its substantive limb due to ill-treatment in police custody and under its procedural limb due to ineffective investigation.

anchor.surface_text: Articles 6 and 13 of the Convention

concepts.interpretation: The applicant complained under Article 6 that he had no opportunity to bring compensation proceedings due to lack of effective investigation. The Court found no need to examine this separately given the violation of Article 3 substantive and procedural limbs.

anchor.surface_text: Articles 6 and 13 of the Convention

concepts.interpretation: The applicant complained under Article 13 that domestic authorities failed to conduct an effective investigation into his allegations. The Court examined these complaints from the standpoint of Article 3 alone.

anchor.surface_text: Article 3 enshrines one of the most fundamental values of democratic societies, making no provision for exceptions, and no derogation from it is permissible under Article 15 § 2 (see Selmouni v. France [GC], no. 25803/94, § 95, ECHR 1999-V).

concepts.interpretation: The Court reiterates that Article 3 imposes positive obligations on the State to prevent ill-treatment and to investigate allegations effectively.

anchor.surface_text: standard of proof “beyond reasonable doubt”

concepts.interpretation: The Court generally applies the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt in assessing evidence of ill-treatment, which may also be established by strong, clear, and concordant inferences or unrebutted presumptions of fact.

anchor.surface_text: investigate allegations of ill-treatment when they are “arguable” and “raise a reasonable suspicion”

concepts.interpretation: Article 3 requires authorities to investigate allegations of ill-treatment when they are arguable and raise a reasonable suspicion, with investigations being independent, impartial, prompt, and effective.

anchor.surface_text: the applicant’s representative did not lodge a formal criminal complaint until 11 May 2000, some 18 months later

concepts.interpretation: The Court considered the delay in lodging the complaint but found that the applicant’s allegations were not unsubstantiated due to late complaint, given the five-year time-limit for prosecution and the inactivity of representatives.

anchor.surface_text: Article 3 enshrines one of the most fundamental values of democratic societies, making no provision for exceptions

concepts.interpretation: The Court notes that Article 3 is an absolute right allowing no margin of appreciation or derogation under Article 15 § 2.

concepts.interpretation: The Court applies the principle that investigations must be necessary in a democratic society, ensuring effective protection of rights under Article 3.

FOR THESE REASONS, THE COURT UNANIMOUSLY

1.  Declares the application admissible;

holdings.reasoning_summary: The Court found the application not manifestly ill-founded and admissible under Article 35 § 3 of the Convention.

holdings.text: Holds that there has been a violation of Article 3 of the Convention under both its substantive and procedural limbs

anchor.surface_text: 2.  Holds that there has been a violation of Article 3 of the Convention under both its substantive and procedural limbs;

holdings.reasoning_summary: The Court found that the applicant was subjected to ill-treatment in police custody (substantive violation) and that the domestic authorities failed to conduct an effective investigation (procedural violation) under Article 3.

holdings.text: Holds that there is no need to examine separately the applicant’s complaint under Article 6 of the Convention

anchor.surface_text: 3.  Holds that there is no need to examine separately the applicant’s complaint under Article 6 of the Convention;

holdings.reasoning_summary: Given the violation found under Article 3 substantive and procedural limbs, the Court considered it unnecessary to examine the Article 6 complaint separately.

holdings.text: Holds that the respondent State is to pay the applicant, within three months from the date on which the judgment becomes final in accordance with Article 44 § 2 of the Convention, EUR 7,500 (seven thousand five hundred euros), plus any tax that may be chargeable, in respect of non‑pecuniary damage

anchor.surface_text:
4.  Holds

(a)  that the respondent State is to pay the applicant, within three months from the date on which the judgment becomes final in accordance with Article 44 § 2 of the Convention, EUR 7,500 (seven thousand five hundred euros), plus any tax that may be chargeable, in respect of non‑pecuniary damage, to be converted into new Turkish liras at the rate applicable at the date of settlement;

holdings.reasoning_summary: The Court awarded just satisfaction for non-pecuniary damage due to the pain and distress suffered by the applicant as a result of the violation of Article 3.

holdings.text: Holds that from the expiry of the above-mentioned three months until settlement simple interest shall be payable on the above amount at a rate equal to the marginal lending rate of the European Central Bank during the default period plus three percentage points

anchor.surface_text: (b)  that from the expiry of the above-mentioned three months until settlement simple interest shall be payable on the above amount at a rate equal to the marginal lending rate of the European Central Bank during the default period plus three percentage points;

holdings.reasoning_summary: The Court ordered default interest on the awarded amount at the specified rate until payment is made.

holdings.text: Dismisses the remainder of the applicant’s claim for just satisfaction

anchor.surface_text: 5.  Dismisses the remainder of the applicant’s claim for just satisfaction.

holdings.reasoning_summary: The Court dismissed the applicant's claims for pecuniary damage and costs due to lack of substantiation.

1.  Declares the application admissible;
